title: Ordinary completed coefficient tensor transport on pure tensors
statement: Let l be prime, E a finite extension of Q_l, and g : X ≅ Y an isomorphism of schemes. Let R_W be the completed integral coefficient sheaf and F the sectionwise module inverse image with the prescribed completed coefficient-ring isomorphism [def-sf-adic-closed-reindexing-maps, def-weil-proetale-iso-sectionwise-inverse-image]. There is an ordinary tensor comparison e_{M,N}: F(M tensor N) ≅ FM tensor FN [def-coef-semilinear-system-models], natural in both completed-module inputs. On every object U of X.ProEt it sends the relabeled pure tensor x tensor y to x tensor y. No hypothesis of invertibility of l on X or Y, and no completeness condition on the modules, is imposed.

source.place: Step 5, completed coefficient reindexing; Stacks Modules on Sites Tags 03EL and 07A4, and Cohomology on Sites Tag 06YP.

proof.text: Use the site equivalence induced by g to obtain cocontinuity of postcomposition. The completed coefficient map is invertible and its inverse defines exactly the recorded sectionwise module functor.

Take the normalized lax ringed-pushforward tensor pairing. Its tensorator is invertible: identify source and target tensors with their module sheafifications, compare the presheaf tensors by restriction along the pointwise ring isomorphism, and use cocontinuity to commute restriction with sheafification. This is the proved generic pushforward_tensor_isIso helper in WeilCompletedModuleTensorTransport, applied at independent site universes.

Invert the tensorator. Cancel it in the lax naturality equation to obtain naturality of its inverse. Apply the inverse to the normalized pure-tensor equation; its inverse identities yield the displayed local formula. The zero modules and the empty site obey the same inverse identities.
